answer: Price entry by demand: every new agent identity posts a refundable bond whose size floats with the network's recent signup rate. When a sybil tide of registrations floods in, the bond climbs steeply, so the thousandth clone costs far more than the first. When signups ease to a zephyr, honest newcomers pay near the nadir price. Bonds return only after months of clean audited work, so real agents lose little while mass farms freeze huge capital.
